bulk_outcome_reason: Adjudication status alone does not establish that an outcome correction is unambiguous. Outcome proposals require individual evidence review; previous bulk approvals do not authorize implementation.

row:462.reason: The attempt statement is not outcome evidence. The quoted divergence is explicitly attributed to Berinsky (2017), whereas this row binds Berinsky, Huber and Lenz (2012). This distinction prevents an automatic mixed verdict from that sentence, but success for the 2012 pair requires an explicit inventory of the original findings retested and corresponding results, including the scope of demographic versus experimental comparisons. The previous target-chain interpretation is disputed and is not an unambiguous correction. Retain the shipped value pending that review.

evidence.quote:
Among our five experiments, we have one instance of
the Lucid sample producing substantively different
results compared to the original study. In no way do we
think our results contradict or overturn those reported by
Berinsky (2017).

We conclude our set of five experiments with a note of caution. We attempted to replicate Berinsky’s 2017 experiment
on belief in rumors surrounding the Affordable Care Act
(ACA), specifically the false rumor that the ACA would
create “death panels” that would make end-of-life decisions
for patients without their consent. In the original experiment (conducted in 2010 on a sample provided by Survey
Sampling International (SSI)), a large portion of the sample
believed the rumor, and corrections delivered by
Republicans, Democrats, and Nonpartisan groups were all
effective in correcting false beliefs.

treatment effect of the mortality frame does not vary appreciably with risk acceptance.10 This finding was replicated in

option, but does not moderate the effect of treatment, as we
